I am seventy this year, and I have been looking after our 10.1 mu since my husband fell ill fifteen years ago. My youngest son and his wife live with me, along with our grandchildren, so there are seven mouths to feed, though two of my children work in the city and send money home. That off-farm money helps, but we still depend on the land. My cropping system is wheat-maize double cropping on 7 mu—that is my foundation. I keep 3.1 mu in cotton for extra cash. My back is not what it used to be, so I cannot expand the cotton, but my daughter-in-law helps with the picking.

My wheat went into the ground last October after rotary tillage. Now it is greening up, so I will topdress about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu at jointing—I know the extension fellow says 15 kg, but last year I did 15 and the plants looked a little yellow, so I am adding one more to be safe. I will put down compound fertilizer with about 6 kg phosphorus and 4 kg potassium per mu as well. I will irrigate three times from my well: once now if the spring is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Pumping costs money, so I will not water more than that, but I will not let the crop thirst either. I expect around 470 kg per mu if the weather holds. I use an improved wheat variety; the seed is reliable and I know how it behaves.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in early June—everyone uses hybrid now, the yield is much better. There is almost no time between wheat harvest and maize planting, so I will plant no-tillage. I will apply about 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. Maize needs two irrigations: one at tasseling and one at grain filling. I will spray herbicide once and watch for borers; if I see them, I will spray insecticide once more. I expect about 510 kg per mu.

My 3.1 mu of cotton goes in around late April with rotary tillage. I use an improved cotton variety. Cotton is hungry and fussy, so I give it about 13 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice—at flowering and when the bolls are filling. Cotton pests are terrible some years, so I will spray four times: mostly for bollworm and aphids. I check the plants every few days. If the price holds, I hope for about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu. That is less than wheat or maize per mu, but the cash helps with school fees.
